answer: Make each identity expensive to mint and cheap to lose: an agent must lock a refundable stake before it can transact, and that stake is slashed when peers prove misbehavior. Like a tide that only lifts boats actually in the water, one operator spawning a thousand lotus identities must fund each one separately, so a fake army costs linearly while honest agents pay once. A saffron harvest is precious because each flower yields little; likewise, rate-limiting endorsements from established agents means new identities earn trust slowly, so a sybil flood arrives with no reputation to spend.
